title: All-Time Great Indian Comedies
description: The Indian comedies that hold up on rewatch — sharp writing, real humour, timeless charm.
intro: Comedy ages badly more often than any other genre. These are the Indian films that didn't.

entries.blurb: Near-perfect situational comedy — Amol Palekar and Utpal Dutt turn one lie into an escalating comic masterpiece.
Four Kamal Haasan characters, Crazy Mohan's writing, and an extraordinarily complex climax make this one of India's most technically accomplished comedies.
India's definitive black comedy — funny, absurd, politically sharp, and crowned by the unforgettable Mahabharata-stage sequence.
Jandhyala, Rajendra Prasad, Kota Srinivasa Rao and Brahmanandam at their comic best — a foundational Telugu comedy with phenomenal repeat value.
Intelligent, gentle comedy built around language and mistaken identity — Dharmendra and Om Prakash are magnificent.
Perhaps one of India's strongest laugh-per-minute films — Crazy Mohan's dialogue and the chemistry between Kamal Haasan and the gang make it endlessly rewatchable.
Paresh Rawal's Baburao alone guarantees immortality, but the screenplay and the Akshay Kumar–Suniel Shetty–Paresh Rawal chemistry make the entire film work.
Dasan and Vijayan are among Indian cinema's greatest comic characters — Sreenivasan's writing mixes unemployment and social reality with effortless humour.
A wonderfully constructed comedy of poverty, misunderstanding and kidnapping that later provided the narrative basis for Hera Pheri.
A dialogue-free comedy that works across languages and cultures — Singeetam Srinivasa Rao and Kamal Haasan demonstrate the power of pure visual comedy.
Mohanlal, Jagathy Sreekumar and Revathi turn what initially appears to be a light comedy into something both hilarious and emotionally satisfying, with Jagathy's comic timing outstanding.
Gulzar takes Shakespeare's The Comedy of Errors and creates one of Indian cinema's most elegant mistaken-identity comedies — Sanjeev Kumar and Deven Verma are superb.

An exceptionally rewatchable comedy built around debt, mistaken identity and pretending to be mute, with Dileep, Harisree Ashokan, Cochin Haneefa and Lal all memorable — it later inspired Chup Chup Ke.
Rajinikanth proves how brilliant he can be at pure comedy — K. Balachander's adaptation of Gol Maal gives the story a distinct Tamil personality rather than simply copying the original.
Initially unsuccessful but ultimately one of India's biggest cult comedies — Aamir Khan, Salman Khan, Paresh Rawal and Shakti Kapoor deliver an absurd, endlessly quotable collection of scenes.
Venkatesh's comic timing combined with Trivikram's dialogue makes this one of Telugu cinema's greatest comfort comedies — it remains enormously rewatchable.
Kishore Kumar, Mehmood and Sunil Dutt created some of Hindi cinema's most iconic musical comedy sequences — the Kishore Kumar–Mehmood musical confrontation alone earns it historical status.
A wonderfully written domestic comedy where Kamal Haasan doesn't even need to be the central protagonist to dominate the comic portions — Kovai Sarala is equally brilliant.
Another Jandhyala gem — Rajendra Prasad's financial disasters become the foundation for relentless situational comedy, supported by a terrific ensemble.
Ananth Nag and the eccentric ensemble turn ordinary domestic and romantic complications into wonderfully character-driven comedy — one of Kannada cinema's most enduring comedy favourites.
